title: Inertial Navigation
src: R.K. Bali — Air Navigation, Part II Ch 6

qs.q: An aircraft flies a great-circle track from waypoint 4 (35°00.0′S 20°00.0′W) to waypoint 5 (35°00.0′S 30°00.0′W). With DSR TK/ST selected on the CDU, the desired track displayed as the aircraft overflies waypoint 4 is:

An aircraft flies a great-circle track from waypoint 4 (35°00.0′S 20°00.0′W) to waypoint 5 (35°00.0′S 30°00.0′W). With DIS/TIME selected, the distance to go displayed as the aircraft overflies waypoint 4 is:
qs.ex: Rhumb-line distance = 10 × 60 × cos 35° = 491.5 nm; the great circle is always shorter.

qs.q: An aircraft flies a great-circle track from waypoint 4 (35°00.0′S 20°00.0′W) to waypoint 5 (35°00.0′S 30°00.0′W). With POS selected and the longitude readout showing 25°00.0′W, the latitude readout will be:
qs.ex: In the southern hemisphere the great circle lies on the polar (south) side of the rhumb line.

qs.q: An aircraft flies a great-circle track from waypoint 4 (35°00.0′S 20°00.0′W) to waypoint 5 (35°00.0′S 30°00.0′W). With XTK/TKE selected, midway between the waypoints the cross-track readout will show:
qs.ex: The aircraft is following the great-circle track, so there is no cross-track displacement.

qs.q: An aircraft flies a great-circle track from waypoint 4 (35°00.0′S 20°00.0′W) to waypoint 5 (35°00.0′S 30°00.0′W). The total change in track angle between waypoints 4 and 5 is:
qs.ex: Track at WP5 = 267.13° + 5.74° = 272.87°: increasing, by less than 10°.

qs.q: Waypoint 3 is 55°15′N 178°37′W and waypoint 4 is 55°15′N 171°23′E. What would be the DSR TK indicated on leaving WPT 3?
qs.ex: RL track 270°; convergency WPT3–WPT4 = 0.5 × 10 × sin 55°15′ = 4.1°; initial GC track 274.1°.

qs.q: Waypoint 3 is 55°15′N 178°37′W and waypoint 4 is 55°15′N 171°23′E. What is the approximate distance to go at WPT 3?
Waypoint 3 is 55°15′N 178°37′W and waypoint 4 is 55°15′N 171°23′E. If the INS shows 0 TKE at the mid-point, what latitude should it indicate?
qs.ex: Convergency from WPT3 to the mid-point ≈ 2° over about 171 nm; in the northern hemisphere the great circle lies north of the rhumb line, so the latitude is north of 55°15′ (book: 55°21.8′N).

qs.q: Waypoint 3 is 55°15′N 178°37′W and waypoint 4 is 55°15′N 171°23′E. On reaching waypoint 4, what TMG should be indicated?
At the end of an 8 h 24 min flight, the INS shows 43°01.1′N 27°40.3′E on the stand. The actual stand position is 42°58.9′N 27°45.9′E. The INS error as a rate per hour of flight is:
qs.ex: Error 2.2 nm N–S and 5.6′ × cos 43° = 4.96 nm E–W → 5.46 nm ÷ 8.4 h ≈ 0.65 nm/h.

qs.q: The following WPTs are correctly entered in an INS linked to the autopilot. WPTI 35°00' N 17°30'E; WPT2 40°00' N 17°30'E; WPT3 40°00' N 14°14'E. From WPTI to WPT2, the desired track and distance would be shown as:
The function of the INS stable platform is to:
o: provide a permanently horizontal basis for the system's gyroscopes
ensure the accelerometers remain horizontal and correctly orientated
provide a datum to integrate with the airborne computer

qs.q: The function of the accelerometers in INS is to
o: determine velocities and hence displacement and new position
provide power to the torquers to maintain the stable platform's horizontality
maintain the angular velocity of the stable platform

qs.q: During the alignment procedure of the INS, the aircraft
o: may be taxied slowly but not subjected to accelerations of the magnitude used for take-off
may taxi but not get airborne, as this involves vertical accelerations

qs.q: A TAS input is required in an INS in order to:
o: ensure the system starts to indicate change of position as it moves
provide a datum against which the accelerometers can operate.

qs.q: In a strap-down INS, laser lock is prevented by:
o: Using Gyroscopes to keep the platform horizontal
Using Dither motor to break the lock
Using accelerometers and computers to compensate for delays

qs.q: RLG in IRS is used to:
o: Keep the gyroscopes gimbles free to move in all directions
Enable computer to link up with EFIS

qs.q: A laser gyro consists of:
o: a laser generating two light waves
a horizontal platform stabilized by 'level push button"

qs.q: In order to align a strap down inertial unit, it is required to insert the local geographical coordinates. This is necessary to:
o: position the computing trihedron with reference to earth

qs.q: Sensors of an INS measure:
In ATT Mode IRS provides the following information:
o: acceleration, angular rate and attitude data.
